note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated; the worker section has OCR gaps that have been filled from context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Much larger than the species of Group I and not liable to be confused with them; comparisons with the species of Group II are given under each of those species. Among Group III only A. brevior may be confused with this species: in A. brevior the median suture of the postclypeus of the alate is always distinct, the proportions of the mandibular teeth differ in both castes, and the enteric valve seating of the worker is also weakly divided. Whether the abdomen of the worker of A. empodius dehisces is not known.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity pale yellow, sparse and inconspicuous. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.29–0.30, Pcl/Ri 2.31–2.56; apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.50–0.53, Ra/Ri 0.75–0.76; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, compound ratio 9.87–10.00; apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, compound ratio 11.89–12.78. Fore tibia hardly inflated, Ti/Ty 4.33–4.73, third apical spur small but longer than a quarter of the other two, not reduced. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum slightly longer than oblique, but well to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating dorsolateral in the undissected abdomen, nearly dorsal, distinctly trilobed, the third inner lobe smaller than the two outer lobes, almost entirely sessile and attached to the second proctodaeal pouch; membranous wall of the valve with sparse spinules outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule deep sepia brown, very deep above the ocelli; fontanelle short-oval, half the size of the ocellus or smaller, depressed, yellowish white to brown; mid-spot short-oval, very slightly raised, as large as the fontanelle, deep sepia brown; postclypeus brown to sepia brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark distinct, semicircular, depressed, brown; antennae brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum sepia brown, the transverse dark suture distinct only on the metanotum, weak or absent on the mesonotum; femora brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites sepia brown; dorsal spiracles pale brown; sides of sternites brown, the middle paler, ventral spiracles pale brown; cerci pale yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by two-thirds or more of their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.22–0.24, Pcl/Ra 2.73–3.15, posterior margin arched or regularly rounded, median suture usually absent, sometimes weakly present. Apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.46–0.48, Ra/Rj 0.62–0.70; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, compound ratio 4.54–5.50; apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth slightly longer than that of the second. Pilosity of head capsule dense, brown, uneven, not felted. Constriction between meso- and metanotum not very narrow, M/W 0.26–0.28. Third apical spur of fore tibia distinct, almost as large as the other two.
